Contrary to most people, I actually think the disgust element is a good element in this. It forces the people who enter to labor for the twisted god of the forge, and the process shapes them into something closer to him. That and the crippling make a nice, thematic downside to an otherwise extremely useful object.

I'm similarly interested in what would happen if a regenerating/unusually resilient humanoid got chucked in there, though I can see why you'd want to avoid sticking that in the article.

+1, with gusto.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Although I was rather wary at first (IMHO SCPs referencing the real world are very easy to mess up), this one just works! The chains feel like a good idea too: the whole thing gives off the impression of a place which became so saturated with divine power that it has been keeping up the work even though the gods have long since left. That said, for that very reason I personally would get rid of the comment about reinforcement of subjects not helping against injuries. The forge isn't trying to mould subjects into Hephaestus' image, it's just trying to have them do his work… The injuries are merely a side effect of working with imperfect material, which may imply that tough-enough would in fact do better inside. That of course is how I perceive this SCP.

As for the repulsion thing, it may be a good idea to get rid of it. Myself I have got the concept behind this but obviously it has been troubling many other readers (which I can understand too - after all we're not in ancient Greece any more so why would people start exhibiting ancient Greeks' behavioural traits all of a sudden), and removing it wouldn't really detract from the article. Not to mention that should one share my aforementioned point of view on what the forge does to subjects, the reference no longer really applies.

Yes, that is also a picture from petra, specifically of the famous treasury there. See, petra is a city, not a building.

Anyway, yeh, the image for the SCP is the facade of one of the buildings at petra.

item.content:encoded:
Well I never saw Talos or the Brass Man in any of the lists of Hephaestus's crafts, but they did say he constructed automatons.
The indesctructable metal was going to be Zeus's Aegis, but it's vague enough to be anything really.
The door-frame, door and lock was supposed to be the ones that were made for Hera, and only she could open the door.
And the statue was supposed to be Pandora, as in one of the lists it said that Hephaestus made her by mixing water and earth, so I reckoned clay was good enough to use.

I'll probably add more to the list, or detail it, if I can think of any other ways for people to fail the crafts without using 'died during engraving' again.
